item.title: Microsoft Confirms Hackers Are Exploiting Outlook 0-Day to Steal Windows Authentication Hashes
item.description: Microsoft has confirmed that hackers are exploiting an Outlook zero-day that can expose Windows authentication information when a user opens a malicious file. Tracked as CVE-2026-124194, the spoofing vulnerability was patched on November 10, 2026. Microsoft marks it “Exploitation Detected” and says it was not publicly disclosed before the update.

item.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday for November 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities
item.description: Microsoft has released its monthly security update for November 2026, which includes 1328 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 60 that Microsoft marked as "critical." Out of 60 "critical" vulnerabilities, 45 are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-113971.

item.title: Red Hat Updates python‑urllib3 for Enterprise Linux
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for python‑urllib3 in its Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support, addressing a flaw. The vulnerability, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, could allow attackers to exploit insecure urllib3 handling, leading to remote code execution. Users should apply the update immediately, verify CVE references for severity, and enforce secure coding practices to prevent exploitation.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel Update Addresses Important Flaws
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for RHEL 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions to address critical security issues. The advisory lists kernel vulnerabilities with CVSS scores; no active exploitation is reported, but flaws could enable local privilege escalation or code execution. Red Hat urges immediate application of the update; CVE references and CVSS details are available for further assessment.

item.title: libreswan Update Fixes Security Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat released a libreswan update addressing multiple security bugs and adding performance enhancements for RHEL 9. The update is rated Important, with CVSS scores available via the referenced CVE links, and fixes memory corruption and privilege escalation issues. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:98046 update immediately to maintain system security and compliance.

item.title: CISA Updates Incident Form for Linked Attack Detection
item.description: CISA released an updated Incident Form designed to detect linked attacks by correlating root‑cause telemetry across multiple incidents. The update provides new detection rules and telemetry fields that enable security teams to identify patterns of coordinated activity and trigger alerts. Administrators should download the revised form, apply the new telemetry schema, and review detection rules to ensure timely incident response.

item.title: Turla Malware Exploitation Enhanced by AI Reverse Engineering
item.description: Turla malware, a Russian state-sponsored threat, is now being reverse engineered using AI techniques, according to a security intelligence alert. The AI-driven analysis uncovers root‑cause telemetry and detection rule patterns, enabling precise identification of Turla's command‑and‑control infrastructure, but no active exploitation is confirmed. Security teams should review telemetry, apply updated detection rules, and patch affected systems to mitigate potential compromise.

item.title: OpenSSH, GPUStack Exploited via CVE-2026-123218
item.description: OpenSSH and GPUStack are being exploited via CVE-2026-123218, a flaw that permits remote code execution through malformed SSH packets. Rated CVSS 9.5, the vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary code on affected servers without privilege escalation and has PoC exploits. Administrators should immediately apply vendor patches, update OpenSSH to the latest release, and monitor logs for anomalous SSH traffic.

item.title: SAP Issues Critical RCE Patches
item.description: SAP issued emergency patches for critical remote code execution flaws in its software, exposing customers to code execution via malformed input. Rated CVSS 10.0, the bugs allow attackers to run arbitrary code without credentials, threatening system integrity and data confidentiality. SAP urges immediate application of the updates and monitoring for suspicious activity, as no workaround exists until patches are installed.

item.title: Apple iMessage Group Chat and Bluetooth Vulnerabilities Patched
item.description: Apple patched vulnerabilities in iMessage group chat and Bluetooth functionality that could allow attackers to exploit the messaging service. The flaws stem from improper input validation in group chat message handling and Bluetooth pairing, enabling code execution or denial of service. Apple released an update for iOS and macOS; users should install the latest iMessage patch to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Microsoft Research Detects Sleeper Agents in AI Neurons
item.description: Microsoft Research discovered a way to turn an agent model into a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons to embed a malicious payload. Frontier agents can detect these edits by spotting anomalous neuron changes, allowing early detection before payload activation. Teams should monitor training logs for sudden neuron modifications and use anomaly‑detection tools to mitigate sleeper agent risks.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Security Update for php:8.4
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the php:8.4 module on Enterprise Linux 9. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities in PHP’s core engine, including a potential remote code execution flaw that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code via crafted input. Administrators should apply the php:8.4 update immediately and verify that all web applications are running the patched version.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Update for mod_auth_openidc
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the mod_auth_openidc module on Enterprise Linux 9. The patch fixes multiple authentication bypass and privilege escalation flaws that could allow attackers to gain unauthorized access to protected resources. Administrators should apply the update immediately and review access logs for anomalous authentication attempts today.

item.title: Cisco ISE Authorization Bypass Flaws Exposed
item.description: Cisco ISE and ISE‑PIC contain web‑interface authorization bypass flaws that let authenticated remote attackers modify configuration. The flaw arises from missing server‑side validation of Administrator permissions, enabling crafted HTTP requests to alter file descriptions; exploitation requires valid admin credentials. Cisco has issued patches that address these vulnerabilities, and no workarounds exist; security teams should apply them promptly.

item.title: Python-jwcrypto Update Addresses Moderate Security Issue
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for python‑jwcrypto on RHEL 9, addressing a moderate‑impact vulnerability identified by the product security team. The update mitigates potential misuse of the cryptographic library, though no public exploit or CVE identifier is disclosed. Customers should apply the RHSA‑2026:97858 update immediately to ensure cryptographic integrity.

item.title: Delve Update Fixes Important Security Bug
item.description: Red Hat issued an important security update for the delve tool on RHEL 9, addressing a critical bug that could affect system integrity. The advisory notes that the flaw may allow unauthorized access to privileged data, though no public exploit is reported. Users should install RHSA‑2026:97877 immediately to prevent potential privilege escalation.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Rust-Sequoia-Sq Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for the rust‑sequoia‑sq library used in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9, addressing a flaw that could allow attackers to compromise system integrity. The vulnerability arises from improper handling of cryptographic parameters, potentially enabling unauthorized code execution or privilege escalation.

item.title: Microsoft Releases Patch for Actively Exploited Outlook Zero-Day
item.description: Microsoft released a patch for an actively exploited Outlook zero‑day affecting Microsoft Outlook. The flaw enabled remote code execution via crafted email attachments, allowing attackers to run arbitrary code on vulnerable clients. Microsoft issued an out‑of‑band update; administrators should apply the patch promptly and monitor for anomalous outbound traffic immediately.

item.title: Railway Breach Generates $740k in Fraudulent AI Charges
item.description: Cloud hosting provider Railway suffered a breach that exposed customer authentication secrets and enabled fraudulent AI usage. Attackers leveraged infrastructure vulnerabilities to steal credentials for up to 100,000 workspaces, generating approximately $740,000 in unauthorized AI compute charges. Railway has applied security patches, revoked compromised tokens, and notified affected customers to reset credentials and monitor usage.

item.title: Microsoft Releases Patch for 1,100 Windows Vulnerabilities
item.description: Microsoft issued a Patch Tuesday update that addresses nearly 1,100 security vulnerabilities across its Windows operating systems and supported software. The release includes 63 critical fixes, among them a zero‑day in Microsoft Outlook, and aligns with concurrent updates from Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla. Security teams should apply the patches promptly to mitigate the identified weaknesses and maintain system integrity.

item.title: US Soldier Arrested in UK for Alleged Russian Espionage
item.description: A U.S. Army member was arrested by British counterterrorism police in cooperation with U.S. authorities including the FBI and military. The arrest relates to allegations of spying for Russia. The Metropolitan Police confirmed the coordinated investigation. This case highlights ongoing international efforts to counter foreign intelligence operations conducted by service members.

item.title: Artex Forks Enable Rapid Credential Attacks
item.description: Forks of the open-source Artex framework and 45 similar pen‑testing tools can execute credential attacks and cloud breaches at machine speed across multiple industries. The tools exploit weak authentication and misconfigured cloud services, allowing attackers to harvest credentials and compromise cloud resources without user interaction. Security teams should audit cloud configurations, enforce multi‑factor authentication, and monitor for anomalous credential‑exfiltration activity.

item.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday Exceeds 1,000 Vulnerabilities
item.description: Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday released 1,093 fixes, with the most attention on an exploited Outlook vulnerability. The update list exceeded 1,000 bugs for the second consecutive month, reflecting a high volume of security issues. Administrators should review the advisory and apply all relevant patches in a timely manner to maintain system integrity.

item.title: Nitori Exposes 37.6M Customer Records Theft
item.description: Nitori, a major Japanese furniture retailer, discovered attackers accessed a system on its network and may have stolen 37.62 million customer records. The breach exposed personal identifiers, purchase histories, and contact information, though the full scope of compromised data remains unclear. Nitori should conduct a forensic investigation, notify affected customers, and strengthen network segmentation and access controls.

item.title: Aurora ADTP Blocks Ransomware with AI in Real Time
item.description: Aurora Adaptive Threat Protection (ADTP) employs AI‑powered intent detection to identify ransomware and advanced threats before they reach endpoints. The system analyzes traffic patterns and user behavior, flagging malicious payloads and command‑and‑control communications with high accuracy. Security teams should integrate ADTP into existing SIEM pipelines and enable real‑time alerting to maintain continuous protection.

item.title: F-Secure Maps 26 AI Harms in Consumer Taxonomy
item.description: F-Secure introduced an AI Harms Taxonomy identifying 26 operational mechanisms that pose risks to consumers interacting with artificial intelligence systems. The framework maps attack vectors moving through AI infrastructure, ranging from misleading chatbot outputs to compromised autonomous software agents. According to F-Secure, the study highlights specific intervention points where defensive controls can mitigate consumer harm across AI deployments.

item.title: Checkmarx Names Kobi Sivilya as Chief Information Security Officer
item.description: Application security vendor Checkmarx announced the appointment of Kobi Sivilya as its new Chief Information Security Officer. The executive transition aims to reinforce internal security posture and guide organizational cybersecurity strategy amid AI-driven shifts in software development. Sivilya will oversee enterprise defense operations and risk management frameworks across the vendor's software security product portfolio.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Low‑Impact DHCP Security Update
item.description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 receives a DHCP security update addressing multiple bugs and enhancements. The advisory rates the update as Low impact, with CVSS scores linked to individual CVE references for detailed severity. Administrators should apply the latest dhcp package via yum or dnf to ensure patched configurations and mitigate potential exploitation.

System administrators running affected Red Hat Enterprise Linux installations should apply the newly available rhc package update to mitigate risk.

item.title: CVE-2026-124848: Kiro CLI Default Permissions Expose Sessions
item.description: CVE-2026-124848 reveals that Kiro CLI versions before 2.27.0 create session transcript files with world‑readable permissions on macOS and Linux. The flaw allows any local user to read credentials, source code, and other sensitive data stored in the prompt history, potentially enabling credential theft. Users should upgrade to Kiro CLI 2.27.0 or later, or manually change file permissions to restrict access.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Update for Enterprise Linux 9
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 9 addressing multiple security issues. Product Security rated the update as Important, and CVSS base scores are provided for each CVE linked in the references. Security teams should apply the patch promptly to mitigate the identified kernel vulnerabilities, maintain system integrity, and ensure compliance with security policies.

item.title: Microsoft Issues Windows 10 KB5131096 Security Update
item.description: Microsoft released Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update addressing multiple vulnerabilities in the operating system. The update incorporates November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes and bug corrections, mitigating potential exploitation paths by tightening system integrity checks. Users should install the KB5131096 package via Windows Update or manual download to ensure protection against the addressed flaws.

item.title: Chrome Stable 158 Released for iOS
item.description: Google released Chrome Stable 158 (158.0.8127.32) for iOS, adding stability and performance improvements. The update does not introduce new security features but addresses minor bugs identified in the previous release. Users can download the update from the App Store within hours of release to maintain current browser functionality and security patches.

item.title: USN-9037-1: HPLIP vulnerabilities
item.description: An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause a denial of service, expose sensitive information or execute arbitrary code. (CVE-2026-91097) It was discovered that HPLIP did not properly handle certain input, which could result in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue only affected Ubuntu 16.04 LTS and Ubuntu 18.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-91100) It was discovered that HPLIP did not properly validate certain array indices.

item.title: Hackers exploit trusted AWS access to breach multiple cloud environments
item.description: A threat actor used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials for a Qubole big data platform's AWS account to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers' AWS environments. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-126087.

item.title: Git Patches Flaw That Lets Malicious Repositories Execute Code During Recursive Clones
item.description: A flaw in Git can let a malicious repository run an attacker's code on a computer that clones it recursively, together with its submodules. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-111760, is an integer truncation in how Git handles its index.

item.title: Microsoft Aware of Exploited Outlook Zero-Day CVE-2026-124194
item.description: Microsoft reports active exploitation of Outlook zero‑day CVE‑2026‑124194, found among 1,094 vulnerabilities patched in its November 2026 update. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution via malformed email attachments, scoring CVSS 10.0 and enabling arbitrary code on affected systems. Microsoft released a patch in the November 2026 Rollup; administrators should apply it immediately and monitor mail traffic for anomalous attachments.

item.title: SGLang RCE Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data
item.description: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, running arbitrary code on a NEAR AI inference server. The breach exposed data from 18 agents and about 100 users, including confidential requests processed in a trusted execution environment. NEAR AI applied a patch to SGLang and recommends updating to the latest version while monitoring logs for anomalous activity.
